newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-SCHALKE GIVES THON SOMETHING BAYERN NEVER COULD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCHALKE GIVES THON SOMETHING BAYERN NEVER COULD.

text.p: Olaf Thon enjoyed his days at the heart of the Bayern Munich defence but the little libero has acheieved something at Schalke he never managed at Germany's most glamorous club.
At the age of 31, Thon will play in his first European club final thanks to Schalke's 2-0 win after extra time in Tuesday's UEFA Cup semifinal second leg against Tenerife.
The little-known team from Germany's Ruhr Valley industrial heartland face Internazionale of Milan.

It will be Schalke's first European final in their 93-year history and Thon is already looking forward to returning to the San Siro stadium -- a venue he knows from his time at Bayern and with the German national side.

"It's one of the most beautiful stadiums in the world and the fact we now have the chance to play there is the icing on the cake," said Thon, one of the few Schalke players who would be recognised outside the club's home town of Gelsenkirchen.
Schalke have always been one of the best supported clubs in the Bundesliga but their performances over the past few decades have rarely lived up to their fans' aspirations.
The club won their last league championship in 1958 and their most recent trophy was the German Cup in 1972.

But their record in the UEFA Cup this season has been impressive -- they have won all of their home games without conceding a single goal. Spain's Valencia, Trabzonspor of Turkey and Bruges of Belgium have been among their victims.
Thon has fond memories of Italy as a member of Germany's 1990 World Cup winning squad but he is realistic about Schalke's chances against the mighty Inter.
"We'll be the outsiders, as we are in practically every game," he said. "But we can move moutains with our will to win."
That will to win was evident in Tuesday's match, where a battling performance and headed goals from Thomas Linke and Marc Wilmots -- both set up by Thon -- powered them past Tenerife.
The German press have dubbed Schalke the "eurofighters" for the never-say-die spirit in their UEFA Cup campaign. But Thon says there is more to Schalke than that.
"I don't think people should concentrate too much on our ability to battle," he said. "We have great individual players."

Thon began his senior playing career at Schalke before moving to Bayern. He admits the prospect of a European final was the last thing on his mind when he moved back to Gelsenkirchen in 1994. "I wouldn't even have dreamed of it," he said.
